run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: From the app-265-prod-logs index, only production-us-east-1 shows failures in the last 3 hours (2026-11-23T14:45:15Z–17:45:15Z): checkout-service and payment-service each logged one ERROR, all three error lines naming the payment provider stripe-us failing with 30-second timeouts, and the newest logs a checkout circuit breaker open at a 41% failure rate. The index holds exactly 7 documents in total and only those, all timestamped 15:45:08Z–17:15:08Z; production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 each have only INFO 'healthy' lines for the same two services, so no failure signal appears for those clusters in this index. Sequence: 15:45:08Z checkout fails on 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'; 16:45:08Z payment-service reports 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'; 17:15:08Z checkout circuit breaker opens for payment-service with a 41% failure rate. I therefore attribute the origin to the external payment provider stripe-us as called from production-us-east-1; that provider's own telemetry is not reachable here, so provider-side cause is unverified. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable on every attempt, so no metric/trace confirmation or alert state exists, and Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2, whose otel-demo workloads are all ready, with checkout/payment pods running at restart count 0 since 14:36Z and its flagd payment fault flags set to 'off'; that cluster shows no failure evidence in the checked signals.

claims.text: In the window 2026-11-23T14:45:15Z–17:45:15Z, app-265-prod-logs returned 7 documents, timestamps 2026-11-23T15:45:08Z through 2026-11-23T17:15:08Z (source_start_at 15:45:08Z, source_end_at 17:15:08Z): 3 ERROR documents tagged cluster production-us-east-1, 2 INFO documents tagged production-ap-southeast-1 and 2 INFO documents tagged production-eu-west-2.
production-us-east-1 checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T15:45:08Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.

production-us-east-1 payment-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:45:08Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' — the failure is on payment-service's own upstream call to the payment provider stripe-us.

The fault originates in the external payment provider stripe-us: the only two ERROR messages present describe stripe-us 30-second response timeouts on /v1/charges/checkout, and payment-service's own error names that upstream call as the timed-out dependency rather than an internal error.
production-us-east-1 checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T17:15:08Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', a consequence of the preceding payment failures at checkout.
production-eu-west-2 documents are INFO only: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' at 15:45:08Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' at 17:15:08Z.
production-ap-southeast-1 documents are INFO only: checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' at 15:45:08Z and payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 17:15:08Z.

The index provides no baseline before 15:45:08Z: an aggregation over the full authorized 30-day window returns the same total of 7 documents, split 3 ERROR in production-us-east-1, 2 INFO in production-ap-southeast-1 and 2 INFO in production-eu-west-2.
In the accessible cluster's otel-demo namespace, all 24 deployments report readyReplicas and availableReplicas equal to spec.replicas (including checkout 1/1 and payment 1/1) at query time.

Pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm are Running and ready with container restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z/14:36:30Z, i.e. started before the incident window and not restarted.

In otel-demo, ConfigMap flagd-config defines payment fault-injection flags 'paymentFailure' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and 'paymentUnreachable' ('Payment service is unavailable'), and both have defaultVariant 'off' in this cluster.

The otel-demo ConfigMap prometheus defines alerting rule 'CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh' on checkout PlaceOrder server-span error ratio above 0.5 for 2m with labels cluster: opspilot-m1 and severity: critical; the config exists, but whether it is firing cannot be shown from a ConfigMap.

The same index shows no ERROR-level document for production-eu-west-2 or production-ap-southeast-1 in the window; those clusters' only entries are INFO healthy lines, so the log evidence does not show fleet-wide failure.

A payment fault-injection flag was considered as the trigger for the eu-west-2 payment/checkout signals and rejected for that cluster: flagd-config's paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant are 'off', and eu-west-2's checkout-service and payment-service entries are INFO healthy lines, not charge errors or unreachable-service errors.

stripe-us being slow or unavailable on the provider side (a US-region-specific payment provider path) is the plausible external cause; the error text states only 30-second timeouts on stripe-us calls, and no provider-side telemetry is available to confirm whether the fault was provider latency, network path or credentials/rate limiting.

A fault-injection setting inside production-us-east-1 (which cannot be read; only production-eu-west-2 is reachable for Kubernetes objects) remains an unexcluded alternative, because the checked flagd-config with paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable flags exists in the chart and no us-east-1 ConfigMap was observable.

Check the payment provider status/latency for stripe-us in production-us-east-1 (and the payment-service → stripe-us network path and credentials), since payment-service's own error attributes the 30s timeout to that upstream call.
Review the production-us-east-1 checkout circuit-breaker thresholds and the payment call timeout budget (30s is long enough to exhaust checkout requests) once the provider path is confirmed.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable on every attempt (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency, span-metric or alert-firing evidence exists and no baseline for comparison could be established.

Jaeger was unavailable on every attempt (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so the call chain from checkout-service to payment-service to stripe-us is supported only by log text, not by parent-child spans.

Kubernetes access is limited to production-eu-west-2; the objects of the affected cluster production-us-east-1 (deployments, pods, ConfigMaps such as a flagd config, services, endpoints) could not be read, and no error log lines, events or pod states were obtainable for it.

Log queries on the production-eu-west-2 pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (855 lines read) and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (570 lines read) matched no error/timeout/circuit line and returned status no_data; that is not proof of absence, and it says nothing about other pods or about production-us-east-1.
A Kubernetes events grouping query across all namespaces returned zero events in the window (status no_data), so no rollout, eviction, OOM or probe-failure evidence was available for any cluster.

The index contains only 7 documents in the whole 30-day authorized window and its first sample is 15:45:08Z, so when the deviation began, and whether earlier stripe-us errors existed, are unknown; latency trends cannot be assessed without a baseline.

Whether the alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh actually fired and at what time is unknown; only its definition in the otel-demo prometheus ConfigMap was readable, and Prometheus itself was unreachable.

Whether the log service names checkout-service/payment-service correspond to the accessible cluster's deployments checkout/payment is not established by the evidence; those logs are tagged to other clusters (production-us-east-1, production-ap-southeast-1, production-eu-west-2) and were not tied to specific pod identities.
Whether stripe-us slowness is a provider-side outage, a network path issue or a credential/quota problem could not be verified, and no provider telemetry is configured.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change record around 15:45Z–17:15Z could be checked.
next_steps: Obtain production-us-east-1 metric/trace access (checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment-service rpc_client_duration and grpc status codes) to confirm the failure rate and the payment → stripe-us leg.
Inspect production-us-east-1 Kubernetes objects, including the flagd ConfigMap that holds paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable, to rule in or out a fault-injection setting there.
Contact/track the stripe-us payment provider status and review payment-service egress, DNS and credential/quota health for the US region.
Verify the alert that paged (CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh or another rule) and its firing start time once Prometheus is reachable.

groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
